clue.text: Ham bone I cooked in unconventional way

indicators.note: cooked suggests the ingredients are worked over and mixed, so these letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A recipe note: a ham bone has been cooked in an odd, unorthodox fashion.
explanation.walkthrough: 'cooked' shuffles HAM BONE I; 'in' and 'way' merely link the anagram to the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: a bohemian lifestyle is one that ignores social conventions, as artists' lives were said to.

clue.text: Go over someone's head, being close to exam result

parts.note: by means near or close to, as in 'stand by me'
a pass is a successful result in an exam

explanation.surface: A student hopes to leapfrog authority because the exam result is nearly in.
explanation.definitionFit: Idiom: to bypass someone is to go past them to a higher authority, ignoring their rank.

clue.text: People with complaints may resort to these

definitions.text: People with complaints may resort to these

parts.words: People with complaints may resort to these
parts.note: complaints are ailments, not grievances, and a resort is a spa town; invalids went to spa establishments for water cures

explanation.surface: Disgruntled customers have certain options they might turn to.
explanation.walkthrough: 'complaints' suggests grumbling, but here means illnesses; 'resort' hints at a health resort.
explanation.definitionFit: Hydros are hotels or spas offering hydropathic water treatments, visited by the unwell.

clue.text: The form aims often may make

definitions.text: The form aims often may make

indicators.note: the letters given may make something else when reorganised, which signals rearranging them

explanation.surface: A remark that goals are often set out in a particular document.
explanation.walkthrough: 'may make' rearranges AIMS OFTEN; the whole clue also describes the answer, since aims are commonly published this way.
explanation.definitionFit: A political party's manifesto is a public declaration of its intentions and policies.

clue.text: One really frightened proceeded quickly in drawing a crowd around

indicators.note: in places the word for moving quickly inside the word for drawing

parts.note: drawing is a form of art
ran means went fast

indicators.note: around suggests the letters are moved about and rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone sketching nervously dashed through a gathering of onlookers.
explanation.walkthrough: 'drawing' looks like pulling a crowd in, but it is the noun for sketching; 'in' is the container signal and 'around' the anagram one. Arrant means utter or out-and-out.
explanation.definitionFit: An arrant coward is an utter, out-and-out one, a person who is thoroughly fearful.

clue.text: Leave the City in the wet

indicators.note: in places the City's abbreviation inside the word for wet

parts.note: the wet means damp conditions
EC is the postcode area of the City of London

explanation.surface: Someone abandons London's financial district in the rain.
explanation.walkthrough: 'the City' is London's financial district, whose postcodes begin EC.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: to decamp is to depart suddenly, often secretly.

clue.text: Agitated nun that is upset about the tedium of life

indicators.note: about means surrounding, so the reversed abbreviation goes round the other letters
upset in a down clue means turned upside down, so the letters read backwards

parts.note: i.e. is the abbreviation of id est, meaning that is

indicators.note: agitated means stirred up, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A troubled nun is distressed by how dull life is.
explanation.walkthrough: 'upset' turns IE to EI in this down clue, and 'about' wraps that round the 'Agitated' nun; 'upset' and 'Agitated' both read as emotional states in the surface.
explanation.definitionFit: Ennui is listless weariness and boredom, a sense that life is dull.

clue.text: Scholarly in theory

explanation.definitionFit: The word describes learned study and also a matter with no practical relevance.

clue.text: Ruination of parties, a hanger-on can be

indicators.note: ruination wrecks things, so the letters are broken up and reassembled

explanation.surface: A freeloader who turns up uninvited can spoil a party.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Ruination of' rearranges PARTIES A.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: a parasite lives off others without giving anything back, like a sponger.

clue.text: Still room to absorb education that's hair-splitting

indicators.note: to absorb means to take in, so the pantry holds the education abbreviation

parts.note: a stillroom is a household storeroom for preserves, a kind of pantry

explanation.surface: A quiet room soaks up learning that is fussily precise.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Still room' reads as a silent room, but a stillroom is an old household storeroom.
explanation.definitionFit: Pedantry is excessive concern with minor details, the essence of quibbling over trifles.

clue.text: Not just an international trade show

parts.note: the UN, United Nations, is the international body
a fair is an exhibition of goods for trade

explanation.surface: A global trade exhibition is criticised as inequitable.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: unfair means not equitable or right, the opposite of just.

clue.text: I accept order mistakenly and went to and fro

indicators.note: mistakenly means wrongly put together, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone admits to getting an instruction wrong, then dithers.
explanation.walkthrough: 'mistakenly' rearranges I ACCEPT ORDER.
explanation.definitionFit: Mechanically, a reciprocating part moves backwards and forwards, as a piston does.

clue.text: Speak mockingly about food

definitions.meaning: slang for grub, as a noun

explanation.surface: Someone sneers at what is on the menu.
explanation.definitionFit: The word means to deride, and also, informally, food or a hearty meal.

clue.text: Denis seen to be wanting

indicators.note: to be suggests the letters are to become something else, a loose signal to rearrange them

explanation.surface: A man named Denis is apparently lacking something.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to be' loosely signals rearranging DENIS SEEN; 'wanting' is read as a noun, the state of want.
explanation.definitionFit: Neediness is a state of poverty or lack, of being in want.

clue.text: Breakdown expert?

parts.note: suggests a mechanic who fixes car breakdowns, but means someone treating nervous breakdowns

explanation.surface: A motoring recovery specialist.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Breakdown' points to cars; the expert treats mental collapse instead.
explanation.definitionFit: A doctor specialising in mental illness treats patients after a nervous collapse.

clue.text: Youngsters eat greens for development

indicators.note: development means growing into a new form, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Children are told to eat their vegetables so they grow properly.
explanation.walkthrough: 'for development' rearranges EAT GREENS.
explanation.definitionFit: Example: adolescents aged thirteen to nineteen are young people.

clue.text: Sayings in page's rim need translating

indicators.note: translating turns words into a different form, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Quotations written in the margin of a page require translation.
explanation.walkthrough: 'need translating' rearranges PAGE'S RIM.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: epigrams are short, witty remarks or pithy expressions.

clue.text: Denied having fed pig inside

indicators.note: inside puts the word for a pig within the word for fed

parts.note: dined means ate, was fed
a sow is a female pig

explanation.surface: Someone refused to admit feeding a pig indoors.
explanation.walkthrough: 'inside' seems to say where the pig was fed, but it is the container signal; 'having' is only a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: to disown is to deny any connection with or responsibility for something.

clue.text: Key man in the penal system

definitions.text: Key man in the penal system

parts.words: Key man in the penal system
parts.note: key man reads as an important figure, but literally means the man who holds the keys in a jail

explanation.surface: An influential figure in criminal justice.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Key' seems to mean important; it is literal, for the keys to the cells.
explanation.definitionFit: A jail guard carries the keys that lock and unlock inmates' cells.

clue.text: Cause irritation right on the joint

parts.note: the ankle is the joint between leg and foot

explanation.surface: A sore spot on the right ankle is bothersome.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: something that rankles causes lasting resentment or annoyance.

clue.text: Jumps at openings

explanation.definitionFit: The word means sudden jerks of surprise, and also beginnings.

clue.text: Eric got me confused just using simple figures

indicators.note: confused means jumbled, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Eric bewildered me by drawing only basic shapes.
explanation.walkthrough: 'confused' rearranges ERIC GOT ME; 'just' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: A geometric design is made of regular shapes such as circles, squares and triangles.

clue.text: Keyhole operation?

parts.note: E is a musical key
a vent is an opening or hole

explanation.surface: A query about minimally invasive surgery.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Keyhole operation' suggests surgery; it splits into a key and a hole. The question mark flags the loose definition.
explanation.definitionFit: An event is an occurrence or happening, loosely an operation or undertaking.

clue.text: A great stop for sailors

parts.note: vast means very great in size

explanation.surface: A seafaring halt of considerable importance.
explanation.definitionFit: Nautical command: sailors shout it to mean cease or hold.

clue.text: British sailors occupy a border town on the Rhine

indicators.note: to occupy is to be inside something, so the sailors go within the other letters

parts.note: a hem is the edge or border of cloth
RN is the Royal Navy

explanation.surface: Royal Navy sailors seize a frontier settlement on the river.
explanation.walkthrough: 'occupy' reads as military seizure but signals the sailors going inside the other letters; 'border town' tempts as the definition, but border is a piece.
explanation.definitionFit: Example: the Dutch town of Arnhem stands on the Lower Rhine, scene of a 1944 battle.

clue.text: Someone not suited for running

parts.note: seems to mean someone unfit for running, but literally means someone with no suit on who runs

explanation.surface: A person ill-equipped for athletics.
explanation.walkthrough: 'not suited' reads as unsuitable; it means unclothed.
explanation.definitionFit: A person who runs naked through a public place, typically at a sporting event.

clue.text: Cool way to use barbiturates

definitions.meaning: to calm with a drug, as a verb

explanation.definitionFit: The word means calm and unhurried, and also to calm someone with a tranquillising drug.

clue.text: His Greek island tour became quite an epic

definitions.text: His Greek island tour became quite an epic

parts.words: His Greek island tour became quite an epic
parts.note: describes the hero of Homer's poem, whose ten-year voyage home to Ithaca is told in an epic

explanation.surface: A holidaymaker's Aegean trip turned into a long saga.
explanation.walkthrough: 'quite an epic' reads as casual exaggeration; it is literally Homer's epic poem.
explanation.definitionFit: The king of Ithaca whose long wanderings are the subject of Homer's Odyssey.
